descriptionChirho: Prepositional use of the accusative of charis, functioning as an improper preposition meaning 'because of,' 'for the sake of,' or 'on account of.' Used consistently across the NT epistles (Gal 3:19, 1 Tim 5:14, Tit 1:5, 1:11, 1 John 3:12, Jude 16) and in Luke 7:47 (where it introduces the ground or reason for an action). All multilingual signatures converge on the causal/purposive meaning: German 'um willen,' Arabic 'bi-sabab / li-ajl,' Hebrew 'biglal / bishvil,' Korean 'ttaemune / wihayeo,' Spanish 'por causa de.' The English glosses vary between 'because of,' 'for sake,' and 'grace' (Luke 7:47), but contextually all express the same causal/purposive prepositional function rather than the noun sense of 'grace/favor.'
